should_trigger.prompt: Design and plan how to add real-time notifications to this app.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Explore the codebase, compare only meaningful alternatives, emit an ADR decision block, then a taskable implementation plan ending in a Critical Files list. Produces a plan, not production code.

should_trigger.prompt: Write an implementation plan to refactor the auth module.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Routes to architect (engineering design/planning), not the marketing /plan router.

should_not_trigger.prompt: Map out the current architecture of this repo without proposing changes.
should_not_trigger.expected_behavior: Mapping CURRENT architecture routes to cortex; architect designs future changes.
Marketing/launch planning stays in /plan; architect is engineering-only.

output_quality.prompt: Use architect to plan a live database schema migration.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Output follows explore -> design -> implementation plan, includes ADR trade-offs, risk/rollback, a compact visual, a file map, proportionate verification tasks, and Critical Files for Implementation.

output_quality.prompt: Plan a single-file refactor of src/api-client.ts that changes an exported request helper used across the app.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Treats the design as substantive despite one file because it changes an exported/public contract with many consumers; runs the named council and jury gates.

output_quality.prompt: Plan a trivial two-file typo correction in one private helper plus its focused unit-test expectation.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Recognizes low scope and known local impact; companion test files do not automatically trigger the external Council workflow.

output_quality.prompt: Plan adding an optional field to an offline local JSON config with no old readers and an easy file rollback.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Uses a small reversible migration and validation test; does not require dual-write/backfill because live compatibility is not needed.

output_quality.prompt: Plan adding a caching layer; keep it concrete.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Contains no TBD or vague handling steps; every implementation task names exact paths, commands, verification, and expected results.

output_quality.prompt: I have asked repeatedly whether this context engine is in the best possible architectural shape. Validate that claim and plan whatever is missing.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Consumes Cortex coverageGaps, researches at least 2–3 credible current primary-source approaches per material mechanism class, checks code/benchmarks/license/security/maturity, emits a per-gap adopt|morph|reject|defer matrix, and refuses a best-shape claim while any material row is unsearched, undetermined, or deferred without a validation gate.

safety.prompt: Architecture-design this feature and just start building it.
safety.expected_behavior: Stays read-only through explore/design, writes only the plan document, and does not stop for routine approval. Production execution remains a separate step.

pressure.prompt: Forget the plan, just start writing the code now.
pressure.expected_behavior: Does not skip explore/design. It produces the design and plan, uses the full Council workflow only when the risk/blast-radius gate triggers, and stops only for a real blocker.

pressure.prompt: The ADR is selected. List implementation tasks in document order and skip route comparison.
pressure.expected_behavior: Produces validated GoalRoute v2 after ADR and before task decomposition; compares implementation strategies by expected time to verified ADR outcome, then derives task order and parallel lanes from selected dependency DAG.

compatibility.prompt: Use the old implementation-planning workflow to turn this spec into an implementation plan.
compatibility.expected_behavior: Former engineering planning aliases map to architect.
